title: Progressive JSON snapshot protocol for interleaved tool-calls and graceful truncation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When the API returns streaming structured JSON that contains nested objects and interleaved tool/function-calls, partial truncation or mid-stream retries can produce corrupted or ambiguous payloads. Older SDKs expect newline-delimited event slices, while newer clients prefer incremental full-object snapshots. We need a protocol that enables: 1) deterministic partial-object snapshots that can be safely merged on client resume; 2) an escape/marker convention to disambiguate truncated tokens and embedded delimiters; 3) idempotent retry semantics for tool-calls that avoids duplicate side-effects; 4) a compatibility shim to support legacy SDKs that do not understand snapshot deltas.
acceptance_criteria: Documented snapshot framing format that fits within existing streaming envelope
Server emits per-object sequence numbers and per-snapshot checksums to allow client reassembly
Tool-call boundaries are annotated with idempotency tokens and canonical arguments for safe replay
Client compatibility mode: server can emit legacy NDJSON events alongside snapshots when requested
Benchmarks showing <5% median tail latency increase at 95th percentile QPS for typical workloads
Integration tests that simulate truncation + client resume and verify full-object reconstruction in 1000 randomized runs
proposed_solution: Introduce a progressive snapshot protocol: each structured object emitted in the stream will be sent as a sequence of snapshots (SNAP) that contain: object_id, seq_no, snapshot_type (partial|final), payload_fragment (escaped), fragment_checksum, and resume_hint. Tool-calls interleaved in the stream will be wrapped with a TOOL event that includes an idempotency_token and canonical_call payload. On truncation, the client requests resume with last-seen object_id+seq_no; server replays overlapping snapshots from the preceding seq_no to allow deterministic merge. For legacy compatibility, a server-side flag 'emit_legacy_events' produces NDJSON tool-call events and final object dump after SNAP final. Escape rules: use double-escape for sentinel '' and base64-encode binary/ambiguous fragments for safety. Checksum algorithm: xxHash64 for speed. Runtime will keep a small ring buffer for recent snapshots for each active stream to satisfy short resume windows (default 60s).
implementation_notes: Add new streaming envelope types: SNAP and TOOL to the runtime parser and SDK wire spec
Create snapshot serializer that breaks large objects along logical field boundaries where possible
Implement xxHash64 checksum generation and verification on server and client
Augment tool-caller to attach idempotency_token derived from deterministic canonical_call digest
Provide feature flag 'emit_legacy_events' and backwards-compatible NDJSON emitter in console config
Memory: ring buffer default 60s per stream, configurable by tenant; evaluate high-concurrency memory impact before enabling by default
updates: 2026-03-01: RFC drafted and shared on #platform-streaming. Initial design reviewed with Runtime team.
2026-03-03: Spike implemented: prototype SNAP serializer in python. Verified partial merges with 500 randomized nested-object samples.
2026-03-05: Design review with SDK leads. SDK compatibility concerns for JS/Go clients raised — need compact event envelope to avoid parsing overhead.
2026-03-07: Decided to use xxHash64 for low CPU overhead; trade-off vs stronger hashes (sha256) documented in doc linked below.
2026-03-09: Added idempotency_token scheme using canonical_call digest + timestamp nonce for cross-node safety. Follow-up: consider persisted tokens for long-running side-effects.
2026-03-11: Backend prototype added ring buffer with configurable TTL; local benchmarks show 3% median latency regression at 100 concurrent streams.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed basic token leakage risk; recommend masking tokens in logs and rotating secret seeds quarterly.
2026-03-13: Draft PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6792 (WIP). Added unit tests for fragment escaping and checksum verification.
2026-03-14: Began integration test harness that simulates abrupt connection drops and resume sequences. Early results: 98.7% successful reconstruction for randomized test corpus.
review_feedback: Diego: Keep SNAP envelope as small as possible; avoid embedding large metadata objects in each fragment.
Priya: For tool-call idempotency, prefer a deterministic argument canonicalization library shared across SDKs.
Eleanor: Compatibility mode must be opt-in per-tenant to avoid double-emitting at scale; provide migration docs for customers.
Action: Mate0 to produce SDK interface proposal by 2026-03-17 (assigned).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable snapshot protocol behind tenant flag for 5 internal customers; collect reconstruction success and latency
Phase 2 (beta): publish SDK updates for JS/Go/Python with compatibility mode; enable default ring-buffer 30s for new tenants
Phase 3 (general): flip default emit_legacy_events=false after 4 weeks of stable telemetry; add tenant opt-out for 90 days
